rules.justification: Fast mode against the bitwise default (D-122, D-123): the explicit step with every fast kernel of the step, each a chain of fused multiply-adds instead of rounded products summed in the default path's order: the gradient (sum_l U(i,l) B(j,l), halving tree in the default path), D*B integrated per element (sequential sums of r*nn products, then the GEMV accumulation over the quadrature points), and the total-Lagrangian residual integrated per element (the entries of B_L0 + B_L1, the sum over the Voigt components, halving tree in the default path, then the GEMV accumulation). Each kernel entry then differs by at most a few units of 2^-53 relative to the sum of the absolute values of its terms. The explicit lumped-mass step of linear elasticity at 0.8 of the critical time step is stable, so a perturbation of the internal forces of relative size eps per step grows at most linearly with the number of steps; after 20 steps the nodal fields u, v, a, f_int differ by a few eps relative to their largest magnitude. The bound 1e-12 of max|field| (about 4500 eps) leaves a factor of more than 350 over the measured differences and fails on a kernel error, which changes the fields at the 1e-3 level or more.
rules.evidence: akantu-solid tests/fast_mode_gradient.rs, 5x5x5 cubes of tetrahedra (750 elements) and hexahedra (125 elements), 20 steps, small strain and finite deformation, the element-block pass with every FMA kernel, 2026-11-16: largest |fast - bitwise| / max|bitwise| over u, v, a, f_int 2.7e-15 on x86_64 (AMD EPYC 7B13, AVX2 and FMA; a, tetrahedra, finite deformation) and 2.2e-15 on aarch64 (Apple M4 Pro); 3-16 % of the entries bit-identical
